pages.text: "Grandpa, let us go to the hill!" Bouncing beside the stone wall, Pipo kicked the walking stick leaning there. Snap—it broke in two. "Oh... what do I do?" His feet froze.
Fluffy Grandpa Sheep, dozing on hay, did not know yet. Pipo burned to his ear tips. I should say, Grandpa, I am sorry... But his lips stayed shut. He slipped the broken stick into a wall gap.
Grandpa woke. "Oh, where is my stick?" He searched beside the wall. Instead of answering, Pipo turned and walked away. Without the stick, Grandpa could not go to the hill and sat back on the hay.
Mom noticed Pipo's drooping shoulders. "Our Pipo, is your heart heavy?" She sat him on her lap and patted his back. "How can we put the weight down?" He lowered his head without speaking.
Not telling felt like a stone from the wall resting in his chest. Each breath made it press. Pipo murmured, "How do I put this stone down?"
Grandpa limped over. "Pipo, long ago I ran on the hill without a stick. Shall we just go together?" Grandpa offered his hand first. Pipo's heart gave a thump.
Pipo squeezed both fists, gathering courage. One deep breath, then he took the broken stick from the wall. "Grandpa, I broke your stick... I am sorry!" Say sorry, feel lighter!

The stone gently rolled away. His chest felt soft as hay. Grandpa smiled. "It is all right. We repaired it like this in the old days." Mom brought string, and Grandpa aligned the two pieces and tied them tightly.

Tied firmly, the stick could support him again. Grandpa used it to stand beside Pipo on the hill. "One, a big breath! Two, look straight at them! Three, I am sorry!" Pipo recited what he had learned. Crouching beside Grandpa, hands at his chest, he felt no weight at all.

That evening, Pipo nestled onto Grandpa's lap and hugged his neck. "Let us go together tomorrow too!" One sorry after a mistake made the chest lighter. Pipo smiled in his arms. "Say sorry, feel lighter!"
